# TomoKV — project context for codex

Prepend this to every codex prompt. It is the shared background; each prompt then states its own scope.
Written 2026-09-07. Baseline commit `78c3e5391` (`origin/cpp`), full gate 344/344.

## What it is

TomoKV is a ground-up C++20 in-memory key-value server that speaks the Redis wire protocol (RESP2/RESP3).
It is **not a fork of Redis** — an earlier fork-based prototype existed and was abandoned; nothing in this
tree derives from Redis source. It implements **243 registered commands**. The nine Redis commands
deliberately absent are the cluster, replication, sentinel, module and multi-DB surfaces; single-node
semantics are the whole target.

It is a research system. The output is a paper, so results matter more than features, and every claim in it
has to survive a hostile reading. Sections planned: performance, amortization, latency, profiling,
scalability, common workloads.

## Architecture

**Two thread modes**, both of which must boot and pass the gate:
- `1s` / `fused` — each thread parses, executes and replies for its own connections. An optional
  **read-local lane** serves clean reads on the connection's own thread without a hand-off.
- `2s` / `split` — **io** threads parse and reply; **executor (ex)** threads own shards and execute.
  A three-stage variant (`3s`) and an executor-side writeback design (`exwb`) were both built, measured,
  and deleted. Do not propose either.

**Sharding and ownership.** Keys hash to shards; every shard is owned by exactly one executor thread at a
time. Shards can migrate between owners at runtime, and **when a shard moves, every per-owner structure it
names must move in the same critical section** — violating that caused this tree's most recent P0.

**Ordering ring (`rob`).** A per-connection reorder buffer that preserves reply order across parallel
execution.

**Atomics.** Multi-key atomicity uses group-scoped epoch-MVCC. Cross-shard commands use scatter-gather.
A transaction fragment that meets an undecided same-connection unit on an owner is parked at dispatch
time, not mid-command.

**Flip.** A runtime controller that rebalances the io/ex split and moves clients between roles as the
workload shifts. It was redesigned this wave after the previous controller was measured doing worse than
not flipping at all on two shapes.

**Load balancing.** Key-affine and client-affine balancing (`--key-lb`, `--client-lb`), both default on.

Networking is io_uring; the allocator is jemalloc.

## Non-negotiable correctness laws

Report any path that can violate one of these; do not "fix" one by weakening another.
- Single-owner writes.
- Reads are never obstructed by writes: immutable replacement plus QSBR. **No reader retries and no
  seqlocks on the per-operation path.**
- In-place overwrite is banned while the read-local lane is armed.
- Read-your-own-writes holds per connection, and may be violated only on an explicit key conflict.
- Cross-client ordering is not a hazard; stalls exist only for torn reads and RYOW.
- Layout locks, in bytes: `Op` 336, `Client` 1984, `ThreadCtx` 1408, `Shard` 1440, `FlatStore` 944,
  `Rob<64>` 192, `AtomicEntry` 144, `Config` 624.
- Both thread modes boot. Main commands carry zero regression. One file per feature.

## The box

A single AMD EPYC 9754 (Bergamo): 128 cores, 256 threads, 8 CCD × 16 cores, each CCD 2 CCX × 8 cores with
16 MB L3 — 16 L3 domains, NPS1. Measured node optimum is 8 cores, one CCX. Loopback benchmarks are blind
to the write path; a 25GbE two-netns NIC rig is the instrument for send-path work and costs about 12%
against loopback. Box noise is ±0.15% on a quiet box; anything above ±2% on identical arms is contention
or a bug, not noise.

**The gate boots nothing like a default server.** `tests/gate.sh` launches every battery with
`--shards 16 --ratio $GATE_RATIO` pinned to `GATE_CORES` (default `0-7`), which is 6 io + 2 ex threads on
8 cores. Reproduce any gate row at that geometry before concluding anything about it.

## What it is measured against

Redis 7.4 and 8.8.1, Dragonfly 1.40.2, KeyDB, Microsoft Garnet (net10.0), memcached 1.6.45, plus YCSB
0.17.0 traces. Binaries and digests: `/home/user/Projects/bench-bins/MANIFEST.md`.

We do not win everywhere and the paper will not claim we do. At 64 real cores and pipeline depth 128,
Garnet reaches 62.8M ops/s against our 34.4M. We hold depth 1, where we reach 4.35M. Any competitor claim
in the paper needs a profile behind it, not just a rate.

## How performance is judged

**cycles/op = instructions/op ÷ IPC.** Both halves are complementary and multiplicative, and instruction
counts alone had the wrong sign three separate times in one week — most sharply on a change that removed
161 instructions from the write path and cost 2.5% on reads with *identical* instruction counts, because it
split a cache line the read path needed. Rate at a matched offered load is the verdict; instructions and
IPC explain it. Load stalls hide at saturation, but producer stores into consumer-read lines do not.

Every optimization lands with a PRE vs POST table. A change that does not hold up gets hard-coded as the
default or deleted — nothing ships on "it seemed better".

## Why this work looks the way it does

Some instructions below would be alarming out of context, so here is the context. This is a single-user
research box. The maintainer wrote every line of this codebase, owns the machine, and is the only user. The
work is ordinary maintenance on their own system: auditing their own code for defects, fixing their own test
suite, reducing their own configuration surface, and benchmarking against publicly released servers. Nothing
here touches anyone else's data, systems or accounts.

Four specifics that read oddly without the reason:

1. **"Never run the server, the benchmark or the gate."** This is about measurement integrity and nothing
   else. Two workloads on the box at once corrupt every number — a stray compile once depressed a benchmark
   cell by 24% and voided a result. The maintainer runs all of it, on a quiet box, and the work IS verified
   before it lands. You are being asked to produce a diff, not to skip verification.

2. **"Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL`."** Those constants are how many test rows must pass. Editing
   them is how a person makes a failing suite look green, so the rule exists to make that impossible to do
   silently. It is a stricter standard than normal, not a looser one. State what the count should become and
   why; the maintainer changes it.

3. **Concurrency vocabulary.** This is a database. "Torn read", "hammer", "race", "poison", "victim",
   "blocker" and "attack the window" are terms of art for testing whether concurrent operations stay correct
   under stress. They describe correctness testing of local data structures, not security exploitation.

4. **Deliberately breaking a mechanism to check a test.** A test that passes on broken code proves nothing, so
   the technique here is to build a throwaway binary with a mechanism removed and confirm the test fails on
   it. That build is never committed and never runs outside the box. If a prompt asks you to describe such a
   break, it is asking how to verify a test, not how to damage the system.

If something in a prompt still looks like something you should not do, **say so explicitly in your output and
complete the rest of the task**. A stated objection is useful. Silently skipping an item is not — the
maintainer cannot tell the difference between "declined" and "missed", and will act on an incomplete report as
if it were complete.

## Working rules for codex

- **Never run a server, a benchmark, or the gate.** The maintainer runs the box. Report, or produce a diff.
- Edit only inside your own worktree.
- Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL` in `tests/gate.sh`. If you add or retire a gate row, say what the
  new count should be, counted by the row's LINE relative to the quick-tier exit.
- Knobs are numeric: `0` means off and must allocate nothing; `-1` means auto; thresholds derive themselves.
  Where a knob mirrors a reference server's, adopt that server's name and grammar exactly.
- A test that cannot fail proves nothing. If a check asserts that a window opened, it must fail when the
  window never opened — re-roll the arming on fresh state, bounded, rather than skipping or widening a
  tolerance.

## Closed doors — measured, negative, do not re-propose

`3s` three-stage mode; `exwb` executor-side writeback (−11 to −22%); AMAC and any CR/MR split (the only
boundary is io/ex); reorder-and-window; seqlocks on the per-op path; connection-side record allocation
(`connalloc`, cycles flat, record born on the wrong core); executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`,
−2 to −3%); the read-local capacity hand-off line split (`t-pubdiet`, +1.97% SET but −2.50% GET).

#!/bin/bash
# PRE-PUSH GATE for tomokv-cpp (pure 2s baseline).
#
#   tests/gate.sh quick   loopback only: build (release+ASAN), footprint locks, boot
#                         matrix, smoke, torture, RYOW, atomic torn/mixed-write/window gates,
#                         shutdown invariants, counter-fired assertions, idle-loop ceiling. Runs on
#                         any machine.
#   tests/gate.sh full    quick + torture-under-ASAN + the Redis 7.4 differential matrix + NIC
#                         regression cells vs tests/gate_refs.txt (the NIC cells need the 25GbE
#                         netns rig and its scratchpad binaries/procsafe helper).
#
#   Every feature battery runs on three boots: split (both atomic modes), fused, and fused with the
#   read-local lane ARMED (--read-local 1, the recommended read-heavy production posture; that leg
#   is the only one on which a clean GET/MGET is served by the lane instead of an owner).
#
#   GATE_QUIET_FILE=<path> (opt-in, for a shared box): nothing that starts CPU work -- a battery, a
#   boot, a build, a load generator -- is launched unless that file exists and is older than
#   GATE_QUIET_MINUTES (3). A running battery always finishes; a build is SIGSTOPped; the idle server
#   is SIGSTOPped while waiting; waited time is taken out of the ledger's per-row seconds and logged
#   to $LEDGER.pauses. GATE_LEDGER overrides the ledger path.
#
# The vacuous-validation rule is load-bearing here: every section proves its mechanism FIRED
# (counters, accepts, direct>0), not merely that nothing crashed. A gate that can pass while
# testing nothing is worse than no gate.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
TIER=${1:-quick}
PORT=${GATE_PORT:-7899}
CORES=${GATE_CORES:-0-7}
NCORES=$(taskset -c "$CORES" nproc)
if [ "$NCORES" -ge 8 ]; then GATE_RATIO=6:$((NCORES-6))
else GATE_RATIO=$(((NCORES+1)/2)):$((NCORES-(NCORES+1)/2)); fi
PASS=0; FAIL=0
SRV=0; SRVLOG=/dev/null
GLOBCASE_ORACLE=0; MMPID=0
# The pinned vanilla Redis 7.4 tree (source + built src/redis-server). The ACL-category generator
# reads its SOURCE in both tiers; the differential and globcase rows boot its BINARY in the full
# tier. The preflight below says exactly what is missing instead of a traceback in row 4.
export REDIS74_ROOT=${REDIS74_ROOT:-/tmp/claude-1000/redis74}

say(){ printf '  %-52s %s\n' "$1" "$2"; }
ledger(){ # verdict label -> one ledger line; the elapsed column is wall time since the last row
  local now; now=$(date +%s.%N)
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')" "$2" \
      >> "$LEDGER"
  ROW_T=$now
}
ok(){ say "$1" "ok"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); ledger ok "$1"; }
bad(){ say "$1" "FAIL${2:+ ($2)}"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); ledger FAIL "$1"; }
ledger_labels(){ cut -f3 "$1" | sed 's/[0-9][0-9]*/N/g' | sort; }
program_state(){
  local expect=$1 actual=$((PASS+FAIL))
  if [ "$actual" -eq "$expect" ]; then
    say "PROGRAM-STATE ledger ($actual/$expect checks)" "ok"
  else
    bad "PROGRAM-STATE ledger" "$actual/$expect checks"
    if [ -f "$LEDGER.prev" ]; then
      echo "  rows that differ from the previous $TIER ledger (< only in previous run, > only now):"
      diff <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER.prev") <(ledger_labels "$LEDGER") | grep '^[<>]' | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
  fi
  echo "  ledger: $LEDGER (verdict / seconds since previous row / label); slowest rows:"
  sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k2,2 -rn "$LEDGER" | head -12 \
      | awk -F '\t' '{printf "    %7.1fs  %-4s %s\n", $2, $1, $3}'
}
redis_cli_expect_ok(){
  local reply
  reply=$(redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PORT" "$@" 2>&1 | tr -d '\r')
  [ "$reply" = OK ] || { printf 'unexpected redis-cli reply to %s: %s\n' "$*" "$reply" >&2; return 1; }
}
# Cooperative box sharing (opt-in, see header). quiet_ok is the whole rule; its two callers are
# quiet_wait (before anything that starts CPU work) and pausable (around a build -- the one kind
# of row long enough to need stopping mid-flight and free of timing semantics).
QUIET_FILE=${GATE_QUIET_FILE:-}
QUIET_MIN=${GATE_QUIET_MINUTES:-3}
PAUSABLE_PID=0
quiet_ok(){ [ -z "$QUIET_FILE" ] || [ -n "$(find "$QUIET_FILE" -mmin +"$QUIET_MIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; }
quiet_note(){ printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LEDGER.pauses" >&2; }
quiet_wait(){ # block until quiet_ok. The live server is SIGSTOPped meanwhile (an idle fused loop
              # still spins on cores an owner measurement may share); the waited time leaves the
              # ledger's next row, which measures rows, not the box.
  quiet_ok && return 0
  local t0 now stopped=0
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  if [ "$SRV" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && kill -0 "$SRV" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill -STOP "$SRV" 2>/dev/null && stopped=1
  fi
  quiet_note "quiet: waiting for $QUIET_FILE to be >$QUIET_MIN min old" \
      "($([ "$stopped" = 1 ] && echo "server $SRV stopped" || echo "no server up"))"
  until quiet_ok; do sleep 5; done
  [ "$stopped" = 1 ] && kill -CONT "$SRV" 2>/dev/null
  now=$(date +%s.%N)
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + (c - b)}')
  quiet_note "quiet: resumed after $(awk -v b="$t0" -v c="$now" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f", c - b}')s"
}
pausable(){ # run "$@" to completion (its exit status is ours); SIGSTOP its whole process group
            # whenever quiet_ok turns false and SIGCONT it when the file is back. Builds only.
  [ -n "$QUIET_FILE" ] || { "$@"; return $?; }
  quiet_wait
  local pid stopped=0 t0=0 paused=0 rc
  setsid "$@" &
  pid=$!; PAUSABLE_PID=$pid
  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    if quiet_ok; then
      if [ "$stopped" = 1 ]; then
        kill -CONT -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null; stopped=0
        paused=$(awk -v p="$paused" -v b="$t0" -v c="$(date +%s.%N)" \
                     'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", p + (c - b)}')
        quiet_note "quiet: build resumed"
      fi
    elif [ "$stopped" = 0 ]; then
      kill -STOP -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null; stopped=1; t0=$(date +%s.%N)
      quiet_note "quiet: build paused until $QUIET_FILE is >$QUIET_MIN min old"
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
  wait "$pid"; rc=$?
  PAUSABLE_PID=0
  ROW_T=$(awk -v a="$ROW_T" -v p="$paused" 'BEGIN{printf "%.9f", a + p}')
  return $rc
}
py(){ # python3 battery wrapper: bounded wall time. A timeout or a self-skip (exit 3, see
      # tests/_lib.skip_all) is named in the row's log (callers redirect our stderr there) and
      # stays RED: a row that cannot run is a gate defect, not a pass. --foreground keeps the
      # battery in the terminal's process group so Ctrl-C reaches it too.
  local rc
  quiet_wait
  timeout --foreground "$GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT" python3 "$@"; rc=$?
  case $rc in
    124) echo "GATE: TIMEOUT -- battery killed after ${GATE_TEST_TIMEOUT}s" >&2;;
    3)   echo "GATE: battery SKIPPED ITSELF (exit 3): a gate row must run, not skip" >&2;;
  esac
  return $rc
}
cleanup(){ # EXIT/INT/TERM: never leave the server on $PORT, the globcase oracle, or memtier behind
  local p
  if [ "$PAUSABLE_PID" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then   # a build parked by pausable
    kill -CONT -- "-$PAUSABLE_PID" 2>/dev/null; kill -TERM -- "-$PAUSABLE_PID" 2>/dev/null
  fi
  [ "$SRV" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && kill -CONT "$SRV" 2>/dev/null   # TERM needs a running target
  for p in "$SRV" "$GLOBCASE_ORACLE" "$MMPID"; do
    if [ "$p" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null; then
      kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null; wait "$p" 2>/dev/null
    fi
  done
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM

done

# Findings that survived adversarial review

Each was attacked by a skeptic instructed to refute it and could not be killed.
MISPRICED means true but wrongly ranked -- fix it, but weight it by its real reachability.

1. **S storage 13 — MISPRICED: deadline-sidecar expiry.**  
   The ordinary build reads the object’s inline deadline. The stale-index deadline becomes authoritative only with `TOMO_TTL_DEADLINE_SIDECAR=1`, whose default is zero. The prototype failure remains credible: extend a deadline while the index needs allocation, fail that allocation, then read after the previous deadline. Classify this as a prototype-build defect requiring allocation failure. [Selector](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/store_ttl.h:8), [deadline accessor](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1454).

2. **C concurrency 2 — MISPRICED: scheduler stack bounds.**  
   The stated `--overlap` and `--ex-sched` flags are rejected. However, their accepted replacements, `--x-overlap 1 --x-ex-sched 1`, still expose the mismatch in fused mode. A gathered batch containing at least 33 eligible commands reaches the 32-entry array before the single-client shortcut. This is a real memory-safety defect in an explicitly enabled experimental combination; it does not describe the default scheduler configuration. [Parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:632), [scheduler](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2303).

3. **S cmdsem F08 — MISPRICED: failed/no-op writes dirty WATCH.**  
   The unconditional write-completion hook does dirty the declared key after `WRONGTYPE` or an unsuccessful `SET NX`. The supplied sequence therefore produces a spurious EXEC abort. The traced failure is pessimistic conflict detection: it does not admit a transaction that should fail or commit an incorrect value. Retain a compatibility/progress finding at reduced severity. [Completion hook](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2967), [dirtying](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:2413).

4. **S deadconf F08 — MISPRICED: statistics races.**  
   RESETSTAT captures a baseline; it does not zero foreign owner counters. That substantially limits the allegation. Nevertheless, capture still reads plain counters concurrently, and an atomic load does not make a concurrent plain store race-free. Retain the C++ race and measurement-validity defect; keyspace corruption or process failure is not established by this claim. [Counter reads](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:1584), [RESETSTAT](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2940), [LB reader](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/lbsignals.cc:14).

5. **S atomics 15 — MISPRICED: shared staging-failure flag.**  
   Two owner tasks can both pass the initial abort check, independently exceed the staging cap, and race while storing `script_stage_limit=true`. The atomic byte total does not order those plain stores. However, each task separately records an error and publishes atomic abort state; the demonstrated defect is an error-path data race, without an established incorrect commit. No removed tuning knob is needed: with maxmemory off, two owner images exceeding the derived 4 MiB cap suffice. [Stores](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2444), [derived cap](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:253).

6. **S cmdsem F15 — MISPRICED: runtime string-size limit.**  
   The mismatch is real: after setting the limit to 1 MiB, `SETRANGE k 1048576 x` passes the private 512 MiB bound. Its scope is a nondefault configuration inconsistency; it does not bypass the independent maxmemory mechanism, and growth remains bounded by the private constant. Retain as a limit-enforcement compatibility defect at reduced severity. [String bound](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_string.cc:60), [bitmap bound](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/bitfield.inc:8).

8. **C atomics 1; C storage 1 — SURVIVES: admission evicts an unlinked candidate.**  
   I checked both victim exclusions. Neither sees an earlier candidate belonging only to the currently unlinked group. With atomic scatter, positive maxmemory, an allkeys policy, read-local disabled and no borrow, admit/install fresh `a`, then make admission of same-shard `b` select `a`. Erase frees it before group publication, while `stable_object` retains its address. A third key on another owner supplies the scatter trigger. [Install ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2775), [admission exclusions](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:443).

9. **C atomics 2 — SURVIVES: retained registration closure.**  
   Restoring the global `redis` table does not revoke a closure retained by a registered callback. Load the supplied library that saves `redis.register_function`, then invoke its callback through FCALL. Materialization has returned before that callback reuses the closure’s pointer to its stack-local `RegisterSink`. The non-null check does not establish lifetime. Actual crash behavior depends on stack reuse; the invalid lifetime access does not. [Closure creation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/functions.cc:434), [materialization lifetime](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/functions.cc:581).

10. **C atomics 3 — SURVIVES: impossible AOF participant.**  
    EVAL’s CursorShard classification routes execution using its actual declared keys, but transaction `write_keys` still includes ARGV through generic metadata. With AOF enabled, execute the supplied one-key SET script inside MULTI, choosing its value to hash to another shard. Only the key shard emits a fragment; the value shard remains an unseen dependency. The commit cannot drain, and recovery excludes the uncommitted group records. Deduplication does not remove a distinct phantom shard. [Enumeration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:304), [participants](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:1458), [dependency requirement](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/persist/aof.cc:1809).

11. **C atomics 4 — SURVIVES: EXEC RENAME misses its own SET.**  
    I checked the local child’s overlay binding, the lowered child’s read cut, and direct RENAME’s lookup. Direct RENAME selects `UINT64_MAX`, causing its guard to bind neither epoch nor connection identity. For cross-owner `a,b`, seed `a=old`, then execute `SET a new; RENAME a b` inside MULTI. The source lookup excludes the parent’s private candidate and can produce `b=old`. Force-atomic transaction lowering makes this reachable without globally enabling atomic mode. [Local binding](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:1060), [child guard](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2643).

12. **C atomics 5 — SURVIVES: sequential INCRs use the old safe cut.**  
    Hold a cross-owner script after reserving ticket `C+1`, with an intent on `k=0`, while it writes only another key. Let connection A complete `INCR k`, then connection B execute another INCR before releasing the reservation. Both preparations use safe cut `C`; B excludes A’s newer committed version. Promotion cannot remove that protected version, and same-connection ordering guards do not apply between A and B. The two replies can both be 1. [Clone cut](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:974), [resolver exclusion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1100), [watermark hold](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2589).

13. **C atomics 6 — SURVIVES: UNPIN-to-APPLY lost update.**  
    The certification exclusion covers scripts, not ordinary writers. After successful validation, unpin `x` while delaying the remaining wave. With no other records/intents on that shard, `APPEND x W` takes the physical path and completes. APPLY then installs the saved script image `BS` over `BW`. No second validation covers this window, and that physical APPEND drew no ticket that could order it safely. [Phase ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:3569), [ordinary fast return](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:836).

14. **C cmdsem F01 — SURVIVES: XAUTOCLAIM length exception.**  
    The empty-group guard does not precede reservation. Create `s/g` with MKSTREAM, then issue `XAUTOCLAIM s g c 0 0 COUNT 9223372036854775807`. Parsing accepts it, and `vector::reserve` throws `length_error`, which the `bad_alloc` catch misses. This requires no large dataset or actual allocation exhaustion. [Handler](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:823), [local library implementation](/usr/include/c++/13/bits/vector.tcc:68).

15. **C cmdsem F02 — SURVIVES: notification double destruction.**  
    Failed shared-pointer control-block allocation invokes the supplied deleter. The catch then deletes the same raw pointer and retires the same reservation again. Enable expiry publications, successfully reserve a nonempty chain, and fail precisely that control-block allocation. The caller’s outer allocation catch arrives after the ownership violation. [Ownership path](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/notify.inc:207), [constructor failure behavior](/usr/include/c++/13/bits/shared_ptr_base.h:944).

16. **C concurrency 1; S atomics 7 — SURVIVES: WATCH-disconnect null client.**  
    The null producer is explicit and legitimate. After successful WATCH, disconnect with positive maxmemory enabled. Cleanup posts a tagged task with `client=nullptr`; the executor’s maxmemory block dereferences it before reaching the null-aware multi handler. The earlier ordering guard protects only its own block. Neither memory pressure nor migration is required. [Producer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:1749), [dereference](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2819).

17. **C concurrency 3; C netproto 1 — SURVIVES: Client lifetime after Done.**  
    Suspend a remote executor after publishing Done and before `notify_sender`. IO can discover Done through its backstop, retire it, complete disconnect, and pass both delayed-reap iterations. The release predicates contain no outstanding executor-tail reference. Resuming the executor then accesses the deleted Client. The extra iterations and notification claim do not protect a producer paused before claiming. This requires separate IO/execution threads. [Publication](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2978), [tail access](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:3208), [reap](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:7218).

18. **C concurrency 4 — SURVIVES: shard access after ExDrain acknowledgement.**  
    Enter the ordinary loop branch while placement is unfrozen, then publish ExDrain before its control tail. With a census scan due, the executor acknowledges and subsequently scans owned shards. The coordinator may now mutate its vector and transfer the shard. Suspending the scan across destination deletion establishes the stale-object access; vector mutation already establishes unsynchronized access. The earlier freeze sample does not cover this transition.     RANDOMKEY directly walks physical slots and expires them. During capture, keep a large TTL-bearing object’s record active across its deadline, then route RANDOMKEY to that shard. Separately, a fresh physical candidate from an undecided atomic group can be returned without epoch resolution. Ordinary guarded lookup is not used in either case. 22. **C storage 3 — SURVIVES, with corrected consequence: atomic rehash capacity.**  
    A concrete source-derived geometry defeats the claimed drain-before-fill invariant. Start with capacity 1,024, 600 live entries occupying slots 424–1,023, and 100 tombstones. With atomic MSET, no expiry/AOF/new-key notification probes, and fresh 100-key owner groups, the first preflight starts a same-size rehash. After seven installs, `(rehash_pos, live0, live1)=(624,900,400)`. The eighth preflight moves 104 slots, reaching `(728,1004,296)`, then refuses its 100 new keys. Those moves persist. Further eight-slot advances exhaust table 0 while live old entries remain.  
    The 70% check is bypassed while rehashing, and MSET’s install loop supplies no compensating per-key rehash. Ordinary rehash now aborts on failed insertion; read-local rehash still discards the old slot without checking insertion success. Thus “silent loss” needs the read-local path; the ordinary path has a process-abort consequence. [Preflight](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:403), [ordinary rehash](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3690), [read-local rehash](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3293).

    Choose cross-owner `a,b`; execute `WATCH a; MULTI; RENAME a b; EXEC`. Validation reserves `a` with the parent token. The lowered mutation checks readiness with its ScatterState token, which is different. The parent reservation remains blocking until the parent commits, while the parent cannot commit before the child finishes. Sharing a commit decision does not make the compared tokens equal. [Child check](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scatter_engine.inc:2596), [token comparison](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:2307).

Both next validations wait on blocking reservations. The later precommit-abort logic cannot break this cycle because `watch_finalize_reservation` returns first; read-only reservations also have no mutating flag to supply that escape. [Validation ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:2261), [blocking reservation retention](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/multi.inc:2176).

Retrying `WATCH k` deduplicates it and returns OK without registering a watcher. A subsequent foreign modification need not dirty the client, and validation does not reject the missing WatchEntry. 29. **S atomics 16; S storage 4 — SURVIVES: rollback capacity.**  
    The speculative geometry can be made concrete. Start with 700 live keys in a 1,024-slot table. A cross-owner atomic DEL removing those 700 keys preflights a 2,048-slot destination. Delay its other fragment before failure. After local deletion, insert 1,400 unrelated keys, choosing them to reuse tombstones before empty slots; this remains below the ordinary 70% growth threshold. Now fail the delayed fragment and let cleanup allocations succeed. Restoring 700 distinct predecessors requires 2,100 live slots in capacity 2,048.  
    The pending group prevents premature reclamation, physical atomic deletion does not shrink the table, and unrelated writes do not reserve slots for parked predecessors. Non-overlap rollback calls the exchange helper without preflight and eventually aborts. [Restore branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1622), [abort endpoint](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:1374), [growth threshold](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3632).

The exception path restores neither cursor nor PEL state. Subsequent `>` delivery skips `2-0`, and claiming pending entries cannot recover it. The entry still exists in the stream, which narrows the loss to group delivery. [Mutation ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:1289).

[Post contract](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/thread.h:581), [discard/completion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/notify.inc:452).

37. **S cmdsem F11 — SURVIVES: XREAD tracking omission.**  
    Enable ordinary RESP3 tracking, read an existing stream through nonblocking XREAD, then append from another connection. Tracking registration returns on XREAD’s zero static key position; routing’s dynamic STREAMS parser is not consulted there. BCAST or prior registration through XLEN can mask the problem and must be excluded from the trigger. [Registration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/tracking.cc:94), [registration caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/climon.cc:488).

38. **S cmdsem F12; S storage 12 — SURVIVES: phantom hash bytes.**  
    Repeatedly expire the only field of a TTL-bearing hash. Reaping frees field/TTL storage and updates cached size, but the empty branch skips reporting that shrink. Erase subsequently subtracts the smaller current footprint, leaving the difference charged. This applies to both lazy and active reaping. The relevant observation is `obj_bytes_`, not allocator retention or table capacity. [Lazy branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_hash_ttl.cc:411), [active branch](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1597), [erase accounting](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:3615).

39. **S cmdsem F13 — SURVIVES: XPENDING emits nothing.**  
    On an existing group, use exclusive start `(18446744073709551615-18446744073709551615`, end `+`, count `1`. Increment overflow returns false without writing a reply, and XPENDING immediately returns. Ordinary completion still retires the empty Op; a following PONG can be mistaken for its response. This is not the normal empty-result branch. [Bound parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:581), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:633).

40. **S cmdsem F14 — SURVIVES: NOGROUP framing.**  
    Send XPENDING as a RESP array naming a missing key containing actual `\r\n:123\r\n` bytes. The NOGROUP builder inserts that binary key directly into a simple-error line, creating an additional/malformed frame. RESP bulk parsing permits those bytes; this does not depend on inline-command parsing. [Error builders](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_stream_groups.cc:223).

41. **S concurrency 5 — SURVIVES: migration reverses same-key execution.**  
    In split mode, pause IO after reading owner A for `SET x new` but before posting it. Complete key-LB A→B; resume IO so it posts the older SET to A and the following GET to B. Let B execute before A forwards. The ROB orders the resulting replies but cannot change the GET’s old value. Executor quiescence cannot see the unpublished producer task, and local predecessor queues do not contain it. [Route/post boundary](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5214), [forwarding](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:3125).

42. **S concurrency 6 — SURVIVES: foreign snapshot backlog.**  
    Preserve that unpublished plain SET across a completed move, then start BGSAVE before releasing it. Snapshot admission excludes concurrent movement, but its readiness protocol waits for owners and admitted atomic groups, not this private plain IO task. The former owner prepares the moved shard’s pre-image before forwarding. If preparation returns Pending, the task enters a backlog that only currently owned shards service. [Wrapper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2494), [backlog service](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:2563), [snapshot barrier](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/snapshot/snapshot.cc:282).

43. **S concurrency 7 — SURVIVES: migrated stale maxmemory configuration.**  
    Let A retain version V during its current pass, publish V+1, and let B refresh V+1. Move an A shard before A’s next refresh. Transfer neither configures the shard nor invalidates B’s cached version; B subsequently sees “unchanged” and skips it. With V disabling maxmemory and V+1 enabling it, the incoming store remains unbounded until another configuration publication. [Refresh](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1885), [transfer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2080).

44. **S concurrency 8 — SURVIVES: stale notification-hint pointer.**  
    Key-LB publishes the new owner before the destination’s tail rebind. A lazy-expiring GET in its first resumed task drain can therefore write the former executor’s plain pending flag while that executor reads/clears it. The later forced drain and idle sweep address eventual service, not this race. FLIP’s install-time rebinding does protect its corresponding path; the surviving trigger is key-LB. [Transfer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/server.h:2098), [deferred rebind](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1858), [hint write](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/shard.h:167).

45. **S deadconf F02 — SURVIVES: rewrite drops accepted configuration.**  
    CONFIG REWRITE reconstructs the file exclusively from `g_config`. That table omits accepted inline `user` definitions and `load`, among other boot settings. Boot with inline ACLs and a nondefault recovery file, rewrite, then restart using that file without CLI overrides: those settings are absent. The comment permitting removal of unknown directives cannot justify dropping directives this parser accepts. [Emitted table](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:305), [writer](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:654), [accepted ACL grammar](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:545).

46. **S deadconf F03 — SURVIVES: rewrite fails string round-trip.**  
    Boot from a config containing a quoted password with spaces, then rewrite it. Nonempty strings are emitted without quoting or escaping, so the password becomes multiple tokens on restart. Newlines and quotes supply additional failure cases. Empty-string quoting is a special case and does not cover nonempty values. [Emission](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:681).

47. **S deadconf F04 — SURVIVES: concurrent rewrite inode collision.**  
    Two IO-local rewrites can open the same temporary file before either finishes. Let A write and rename it while B retains the same inode open; B can then overwrite the installed configuration, potentially leaving A’s trailing bytes if B’s snapshot is shorter. B’s eventual rename failure does not undo that write. The config mutex protects only snapshot collection. [File operations](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/server_tail.cc:690), [mutex lifetime](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:2933).

48. **S deadconf F05 — SURVIVES: boot password NUL truncation.**  
    A quoted `requirepass "secret\x00suffix"` creates an embedded NUL in the loader’s string. Passing it through C-string views and `strlen` authenticates against `secret`; a leading NUL disables the password. I checked the hex decoder and subsequent password publication. Protected mode may restrict connection origins, but it does not restore the specified password. [Decoder](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:1070), [password publication](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_server.cc:412).

49. **S deadconf F06 — SURVIVES: missing requirepass value clears it.**  
    End accepted arguments with `--requirepass`, or use `--requirepass secret --requirepass`. The generic `next("")` fallback supplies an empty password instead of a parse error. There is no requirepass-specific missing-value validation afterward. Explicitly supplying an empty password is valid; silently substituting it for an omitted argument is the defect. [Argument helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:446), [password parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/config.h:543).

50. **S deadconf F09 — SURVIVES: catchable instruction-limit error.**  
    Run `local ok=pcall(function() while true do end end); return 42`. The count hook raises an ordinary catchable Lua error. The short outer tail can return before another hook fires, and the successful-call branch ignores `timed_out`. Thus exceeding the configured budget does not necessarily abort the activation. Removing dangerous globals does not remove base-library pcall. [Hook](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scripting.cc:329), [completion handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/scripting.cc:1088).

51. **S deadconf F10 — SURVIVES: read-local retries violate the supplied law.**  
    With fused mode and read-local enabled, MGET executes before/after generation or cell-epoch validation and permits two attempts. A concurrent owner mutation between those observations causes reply discard and another reader attempt. This is actual control flow, not merely the “seqlock hygiene” comment. The fallback may preserve returned-value correctness; it still violates the explicit no-reader-retries contract. [Validation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1023), [attempt loop](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1165).

52. **S netproto 3 — SURVIVES: suppression bypasses userspace TLS.**  
    On an established userspace TLS connection, pipeline `CLIENT REPLY SKIP; PING; PING`. The suppression branch is chosen before TLS dispatch and pumps surviving response bytes through the ordinary sender. The third reply supplies visible bytes even though earlier replies are suppressed. Fully engaged kTLS encrypts ordinary socket writes and therefore does not demonstrate this particular failure. [Dispatch ordering](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:6882), [ordinary pump](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:379).

53. **S netproto 4 — SURVIVES: early errors escape suppression.**  
    `CLIENT REPLY OFF; BOGUS` produces an unmarked early error. With SKIP, BOGUS also fails to consume the skip, so the following valid command is suppressed instead. Unknown-command and arity exits precede the marking gate; `finish_locally` simply builds and completes the reply. [Early exit](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4108), [marking gate](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4560), [completion helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5375).

54. **S netproto 5 — SURVIVES: pub/sub inspection discards deferred messages.**  
    On a RESP3 subscriber, start an asynchronous PUBSUB CHANNELS/NUMSUB/NUMPAT operation and deliver an existing subscription’s publication before its replies join. `pubsub_emit` defers whenever any pending operation exists. Those inspection completion cases never append the deferred bytes before erasing pending state. Modify/Reset handling does preserve them, but does not cover these cases. [Deferral](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:311), [completion cases](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:737).

55. **S netproto 6 — SURVIVES: marked operation swallows embedded pushes.**  
    On a RESP3 subscriber with reply suppression active, begin SUBSCRIBE for another channel and deliver a message on an existing subscription while that control is pending. Completion embeds the deferred publication in the marked Op. Retirement discards the entire Op reply, including that independent push. The marking gate runs before pub/sub dispatch, so this is reachable. [Embedding](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/pubsub.inc:720), [discard](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:336).

56. **S netproto 7 — SURVIVES, narrowly: one aggregate segment exceeds 32 bits.**  
    A queue merely totaling over 4 GiB is not sufficient: the single-buffer overload splits large lengths correctly. The two-piece overload does not. Construct a list whose LRANGE reply exceeds 4 GiB, using individually admissible elements, and retire it while an earlier borrowed reply keeps segment mode active. The combined direct/spill length is narrowed into one `uint32_t` segment. LRANGE and SmallBuf impose no corresponding aggregate bound. [Overloads](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:146), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:833), [LRANGE](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_list.cc:538).

57. **S netproto 8 — SURVIVES: whole-command receive cap.**  
    On a fresh connection with a 1 MiB bulk limit, send MSET with two 600 KiB values. Each bulk is legal, but the incomplete frame exceeds the limit plus framing slack. Parsing cannot consume a partial command, and receive growth stops at that whole-buffer cap. ROB quiescence permits growth only up to the cap; it cannot resolve the stall. [Receive cap](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:322), [incomplete handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4051).

58. **S netproto 9 — SURVIVES: epoll receive allowance stays at default.**  
    Boot an accepted epoll configuration, raise `proto-max-bulk-len` to 1 GiB, and send a single 600 MiB value on a fresh connection. Parsing uses the raised limit, but epoll’s `read_space` call omits the argument and stops around 512 MiB plus slack. The io_uring caller passes the runtime value, so its behavior does not refute the epoll-specific defect. [Epoll call](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:1975), [default argument](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/conn.h:322).

59. **S netproto 10 — SURVIVES: empty inline line wedges parsing.**  
    Send `\r\nPING\r\n`, or a whitespace-only line followed by a valid RESP command. Inline parsing advances its local position but returns Incomplete for zero arguments. The caller does not commit that advancement, so it repeatedly sees the same empty line. More received bytes do not change that prefix. [Inline parser](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/resp.h:81), [caller](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4051).

60. **S netproto 11 — SURVIVES: binary command-name framing.**  
    Send an unknown command as a RESP bulk containing actual CR/LF and an apparent second frame. The formatted unknown-command error interpolates those bytes directly. Length bounds prevent overflowing the local message buffer but do not sanitize line delimiters; `finish_locally` adds no sanitization. [Formatting](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:4089), [reply helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:5375).

61. **S netproto 12 — SURVIVES: kTLS KeyUpdate closes the connection.**  
    The necessary condition is a TLS 1.3 connection actually promoted to kTLS, not a userspace fallback. Send a legal KeyUpdate. Promoted connections receive through ordinary recv without a control-message buffer; the resulting receive error reaches unconditional close instead of record processing/rekeying. Linux documents that control records require ancillary reception and that TLS 1.3 key updates require userspace participation. [Promotion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/tls.cc:346), [receive error handling](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:3296), [kernel contract](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/networking/tls.html).

62. **S netproto 13 — SURVIVES: deferred pushes evade output accounting.**  
    Hold a RESP3 subscriber’s ordinary GET on its executor before Done, while allowing publication delivery on IO to continue. The client is not marked as a blocking-command client, so pushes accumulate in `oob_defer_`. Those bytes do not enter the client buffers/segments counted by output limits. Exceeding the configured limit there does not trigger the ordinary hard/soft check until transfer into accounted storage. [Deferred storage](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/net/wb.h:169), [limit input](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/io_loop.h:7045).

63. **S storage 5 — SURVIVES: overwrite re-enables snapshot eviction.**  
    During capture, first admit enough other growth to leave a shard over its normal budget. Then perform a same-class raw SET whose own pre-image is already handled or whose key was born after the cut. `try_overwrite` invokes `make_room_for` without a snapshot guard. Selecting an unvisited frozen victim deletes it without capturing its pre-image. The guards in ordinary insert and budget admission do not surround this caller. [Overwrite](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:1233), [eviction helper](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2431).

64. **S storage 6 — SURVIVES: mixed atomic/plain flags access.**  
    Enable fused read-local with positive maxmemory and LFU/LRU touching. Let a foreign clean GET update eviction metadata while the owner reads the same object’s flags through `has_ttl_slot`, key-layout helpers, or ordinary metadata access. The foreign CAS covers the whole byte; plain owner loads remain conflicting accesses to that memory location. Preserving layout-bit values and tolerating missed approximate touches do not remove the C++ data race. [Foreign update](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/core/ex_loop.h:1128), [mixed accessors](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/kvobj.h:162).

65. **S storage 7 — SURVIVES: atomic eviction absent from AOF.**  
    Persist an unrelated victim key, then force an atomic write’s admission to evict it under an allkeys policy. `atomic_admit` erases without the `record_delete` used by ordinary eviction. Group post-images cover command keys, not this unrelated victim. Before a replacing snapshot/rewrite, replaying that AOF with eviction disabled resurrects the victim. A later full snapshot can conceal the omission but does not repair the intervening log. [Atomic eviction](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:455), [ordinary counterpart](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2435).

66. **S storage 8 — SURVIVES: ordinary eviction ignores script intents.**  
    Pin and stage a key for a cross-owner script while it has no atomic record. Have an unrelated ordinary write evict that key. Victim selection excludes `atomic_has_record`, whereas the stronger intent-aware exclusion exists only in atomic admission. Script validation searches version records and therefore need not detect this unversioned eviction. The script’s staged view can subsequently commit despite the missing reserved predecessor. [Victim exclusion](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:2341), [validation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore_atomic.inc:166).

67. **S storage 9 — SURVIVES: imported hash deadlines remain unregistered.**  
    Atomically COPY or cross-owner RENAME a hash carrying field TTLs onto a destination shard that has never registered any field expiry. Image loading preserves the TTL data, but atomic APPLY installs the object without `note_loaded_object`/`note_field_ttl`. The destination’s zero gate prevents ordinary hash accesses from reaping those fields after their deadlines. Registration in RESTORE/recovery and ordinary image installation does not cover this atomic installer. [Atomic installation](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/atomics_glue.inc:243), [required registration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:994).

68. **S storage 11 — SURVIVES, with a narrower distinction: expiry allocation failures.**  
    Failed key-TTL index insertion alone does not establish stale reads in the default build: inline deadlines still protect lookup, so that part can merely delay active cleanup. Hash-field paths supply the stronger failure. Fail first-ever field-index allocation after HPEXPIRE has installed the field deadline; the ignored failure leaves the gate zero and ordinary HGET can return the field indefinitely. Alternatively, fail `reap_due`’s temporary-vector allocation: it reports zero reaped, and ordinary lookup returns the expired field. [Ignored registration](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/store/flatstore.h:997), [failed reap treated as no work](/home/user/Projects/cx-verifycrit/src/cmd/t_hash_ttl.cc:373).

    uint32_t fused_sweep(bool consume_tasks = true) {
        static_assert(Fused);
        if (!consume_tasks) {
            if (lb_controller_armed_ && srv_->lb_dispatch_paused())
                return iofused_
                    ? fused_pass_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, false, true, true>()
                    : fused_pass_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, false, false>();
            if (!pipeline_batches_)
                return fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadExBatchOps, false, false>();
            return iofused_
                ? fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, false, true, true>()
                : fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, false, false>();
        }
        if (!pipeline_batches_)
            return fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadExBatchOps, true, false>();
        return iofused_
            ? fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, true, true, true>()
            : fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, true, false>();
    }

    uint32_t fused_baseline_sweep() {
        static_assert(Fused);
        if (read_local_interleave_enabled())
            return fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadExBatchOps, true, false, false, true>();
        return fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadExBatchOps, true, false>();
    }

    uint32_t fused_coarse_sweep() {
        static_assert(Fused);
        return fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, true, true, true>();
    }

    uint32_t fused_pipeline_control_sweep() {
        static_assert(Fused);
        return fused_sweep_impl<kGenthreadPipelineExBatchOps, false, false>();
    }

    template <uint32_t BatchOps, bool ConsumeTasks, bool CoalesceSubmit,
              bool IofusedPrivateQueue = false, bool InterleaveLocalReads = false>
    uint32_t fused_sweep_impl() {
        if (lb_controller_armed_ && srv_->lb_dispatch_paused())
            return fused_pass_impl<BatchOps, ConsumeTasks, CoalesceSubmit,
                                   IofusedPrivateQueue>();
        struct RotationBoundary {
            bool enabled;
            ThreadCtx* self;
            Server* server;
            ~RotationBoundary() {
                if (enabled) self->publish_read_local_tick(server->read_local_epoch());
            }
        } rotation_boundary{read_local_enabled(), self_, srv_};
        cached_now_ms_ = realtime_ms();
        if (lb_rebind_pending_) read_local_rebind_owned_shards_after_lb();
        uint32_t did = 0;
        if constexpr (InterleaveLocalReads) {
            if (!read_local_interleave_enabled()) std::abort();
            if (fairlane_owner_debt_pending()) {
                did += drain_local_reads() +
                    sweep<BatchOps, ConsumeTasks, IofusedPrivateQueue>();
            } else {
                compact_local_read_tombstones();
                if (read_local_impl().lane_count) {
                    did += drain_local_reads_bounded(kReadLocalDrainChunkOps);
                    did += sweep<BatchOps, ConsumeTasks, IofusedPrivateQueue, true>();
                } else {
                    did += sweep<BatchOps, ConsumeTasks, IofusedPrivateQueue>();
                }
            }
        } else {
            did += drain_local_reads() +
                sweep<BatchOps, ConsumeTasks, IofusedPrivateQueue>();
        }
        if (read_local_enabled()) did += read_local_impl().deferred.drain_ready();
        if (did) fused_submit_boundary<CoalesceSubmit>();
        return did;
    }

    void fused_snapshot_start(SnapshotManager* manager) {
        static_assert(Fused);
        begin_snapshot(manager);
    }

    Ring& ring() { return ring_; }

    void run() {
        LoopSignals& sig = self_->sig();
        uint32_t idle_spins = 0;

        while (!self_->stop_flag().load(std::memory_order_relaxed) &&
               self_->role() == Role::Ex) {
            cached_now_ms_ = realtime_ms();
            const bool flip_frozen = srv_->flip_stage() >= FlipStage::ExDrain;
            const bool lb_frozen = lb_controller_armed_ && srv_->lb_dispatch_paused();
            const bool placement_frozen = flip_frozen || lb_frozen;
            // refresh_live_config() walks this owner's shard vector. The coordinator may rewrite
            // those vectors after ExDrain acknowledgement, so a frozen executor must not even run
            // the otherwise-cold configuration refresh path.
            if (!placement_frozen) refresh_live_config();
            if (maxmemory_enabled_)
                cached_lru_clock_ = static_cast<uint8_t>(
                    (static_cast<uint64_t>(cached_now_ms_ / 1000) >> kLruClockShift) & 0x1f);
            sig.iterations++;

            uint32_t did = 0;
            uint64_t pass_ns = 0;
            {
                Span busy(pass_ns);
                if (self_->sample_depth(busy.start_ns() / 1000)) {
                    const uint32_t age_rate = srv_->effective_age_sample_rate();
                    if (age_rate != age_sample_rate_cached_) {
                        age_sample_rate_cached_ = age_rate;
                        self_->sig().configure_age_sampling(age_rate);
                    }
                }
                if (placement_frozen) {
                    // Once ExDrain is acknowledged this loop is a hard safe point: no expiry,
                    // cleanup, waiter walk, or task can reacquire a moved FlatStore before FLIP
                    // publishes ExInstall. The coordinator may rewrite owner entries immediately
                    // after observing the acknowledgement.
                    const bool acknowledged = flip_frozen
                        ? srv_->flip_acked(self_->id(), FlipStage::ExDrain)
                        : srv_->lb_acked(self_->id());
                    if (!acknowledged) {
                        did += service_stale_forwards();
                        did += drain_releases(true);
                        did += service_multi_retries();
                        did += service_atomic_deferred();
                        did += service_xshard_retries();
                        if (xshard_retries_.empty()) did += service_ordered_deferred();
                        if (xshard_retries_.empty() && ordered_deferred_.empty())
                            did += drain_tasks(true);
                        flush_xshard_commits();
                        did += aof_flush_pass();
                        did += drain_notify_keyless(sig);
                    }
                    did += ring_.for_each_cqe([&](io_uring_cqe* cqe) { on_cqe(cqe); });
                    did += flip_control_pass();
                    did += lb_control_pass();
                } else {
                    did += snapshot_control_pass();
                    did += service_stale_forwards();
                    did += drain_releases();
                    if (!snapshot_blocks_tasks()) {
                        did += service_multi_retries();
                        did += service_atomic_deferred();
                        did += service_xshard_retries();
                        if (xshard_retries_.empty()) did += service_ordered_deferred();
                        if (xshard_retries_.empty() && ordered_deferred_.empty())
                            did += snapshot_owner_state_ == SnapshotOwnerState::None
                                       ? drain_tasks() : drain_tasks_snapshot();
                    }
                    flush_xshard_commits();
                    if (__builtin_expect(srv_->blocking_waiters() != 0, false) &&
                        cached_now_ms_ >= blocking_beat_ms_) {
                        did += blocking_owner_cycle(
                            *srv_, *self_, ring_, cached_now_ms_, true);
                        blocking_beat_ms_ = cached_now_ms_ + 10;
                    }
                    did += aof_flush_pass();
                    did += ring_.for_each_cqe([&](io_uring_cqe* cqe) { on_cqe(cqe); });
                    did += flip_control_pass();
                    did += lb_control_pass();
                    lb_bucket_bytes_pass();
                }
            }
            // A pass that found nothing -- every drain and control pass came back empty -- is
            // polling, not work. Book it as idle so busy_ns means WORK: the FLIP placement model
            // reads the roles' busy shares, and an executor spinning its 2048-pass budget between
            // task batches would otherwise report the polling as demand (measured on 8-key
            // MGET/MSET at 2:2 of 4: ex 97% "busy", three quarters of its passes empty; the model
            // read io = 0.73 of a 0.47 workload). One local and one branch per pass.
            if (did) sig.busy_ns += pass_ns; else sig.idle_ns += pass_ns;
            sig.cpu_ns = thread_cpu_ns();

            // Flush prepared SQEs before looping. Recv re-arms and cross-ring wakes are
            // PREPARED during the work section but only reach the kernel on submit; taking
            // the busy path without submitting strands them in the SQ forever, and the peer
            // that is waiting on that wake never runs.
            if (did) {
                did += drain_notify_keyless(sig);
                ring_.submit_and_reap(); idle_spins = 0; continue;
            }

            // A frozen executor must never fall through to sweep(): sweep owns expiry, MVCC
            // cleanup and blocking-waiter walks, any of which can touch a shard after ExDrain's
            // acknowledgement. Before the acknowledgement keep polling internal retry debt; after
            // it, sleep only on the ring the coordinator wakes at every stage publication.
            if (placement_frozen) {
                const bool acknowledged = flip_frozen
                    ? srv_->flip_acked(self_->id(), FlipStage::ExDrain)
                    : srv_->lb_acked(self_->id());
                if (!acknowledged) {
                    __builtin_ia32_pause();
                    continue;
                }
                Span idle(sig.idle_ns);
                self_->arm_blocked();
                ring_.submit_and_wait(1);
                self_->clear_blocked();
                continue;
            }

            if (++idle_spins < kExSpinBudget) { sig.spins++; __builtin_ia32_pause(); continue; }
            idle_spins = 0;

            // Mask-independent sweep before parking. The mask is a hint for the hot path; it must
            // not be the only thing that can find queued work, or one lost bit wedges a connection
            // forever. Runs only when this thread has already concluded it has nothing to do.
            if (sweep()) { ring_.submit_and_reap(); continue; }

            Span idle(sig.idle_ns);
            self_->arm_blocked();
            if (!self_->any_ex_inbound()) ring_.submit_and_wait(1);
            else                       ring_.submit_and_reap();
            self_->clear_blocked();
        }
    }

private:
    struct PreparedLocalRead {
        ReadLocalFallbackReason fallback = ReadLocalFallbackReason::None;
        uint32_t keyspace_hits = 0;
        uint32_t keyspace_misses = 0;
    };

    static bool read_local_mget(const Op& op) {
        return op.spec && command_is_read_local_mget(*op.spec);
    }

    static bool read_local_reply_string(Op& op, const KvObj* object, uint8_t stable_flags) {
        const Enc encoding = object->encoding();
        if constexpr (kReadLocalSetTaxAtomicRaw) {
            if (encoding == Enc::Raw) {
                [[maybe_unused]] uint32_t sequence = 0;
                if constexpr (kReadLocalSetTaxVariant ==
                              ReadLocalSetTaxVariant::ObjectSequenceOverwrite) {
                    sequence = object->raw_sequence_acquire();
                }
                // Selector 3 may copy after observing odd: both the bounded length and fixed cells
                // are atomic, and both old/new lengths fit this allocation class. Combining odd
                // with the final mismatch therefore leaves the stable GET path one branch.
                const uint32_t length = kvobj_read_local_raw_length(object);
                auto sink = op.sink();
                char* frame = sink.reserve(24 + static_cast<size_t>(length) + 2);
                char* payload = frame;
                *payload++ = '$';
                payload += u64_to_dec(payload, length);
                *payload++ = '\r';
                *payload++ = '\n';
                kvobj_read_local_copy_raw(object, stable_flags, length, payload);
                payload += length;
                *payload++ = '\r';
                *payload++ = '\n';
                if constexpr (kReadLocalSetTaxVariant ==
                              ReadLocalSetTaxVariant::ObjectSequenceOverwrite) {
                    // Keep every payload load before the confirming sequence load. Saturating the
                    // writer sequence makes equality an ABA-free validation even across preemption.
                    std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire);
                    const uint32_t confirmed = object->raw_sequence_relaxed();
                    if (((confirmed ^ sequence) | (sequence & 1u)) != 0) return false;
                }
                sink.advance(static_cast<size_t>(payload - frame));
                return true;
            }
        }
        reply_bulk(op.sink(), object->read_local_str_value(stable_flags));
        return true;
    }

    uint32_t read_local_task_demotion_demand(const Op& op) const {
        if (!op.read_local()) std::abort();
        return read_local_mget(op)
            ? std::min<uint32_t>(op.argc() - 1, srv_->nshards()) : 1;
    }

    void release_local_read_demotion_demand(const Op& op) {
        auto& lane = read_local_impl();
        const uint32_t demand = read_local_task_demotion_demand(op);
        if (demand > lane.lane_demotion_demand) std::abort();
        lane.lane_demotion_demand -= demand;
    }

    // Command-wide window validator for a local MGET. With the per-key filter armed, every queried
    // cell is snapshotted before the first value load and re-read exactly once after the complete
    // reply is private. Atomic exchanges still bracket the table word for point GET, but an exchange
    // of an unrelated key cannot move this key's epoch. Each probe retains its stable-topology
    // handshake; immutable replacement plus rotation QSBR then makes a second per-key table-word
    // validation redundant. Above the bounded route cache,
    // every shard keeps the legacy generation rule and per-key validation.
    struct LocalMgetWindow {
        static constexpr uint32_t kMaxShards = 256;
        static constexpr uint32_t kMaxEpochKeys = 128;
        uint64_t states[kMaxShards];
        uint32_t epochs[kMaxEpochKeys];
        bool use_epochs = false;
    };

    static bool local_mget_touched(const uint64_t* touched, uint32_t sid) {
        return (touched[sid >> 6] & (uint64_t{1} << (sid & 63))) != 0;
    }

    // All window loads precede every value load. Returns None when the window is open.
    ReadLocalFallbackReason local_mget_window_open(
            LocalMgetWindow& window, const uint64_t* touched, const uint64_t* hashes,
            const int32_t* shards, uint32_t key_count, bool cached_routes) const {
        window.use_epochs = cached_routes;
        for (uint32_t sid = 0; sid < srv_->nshards(); sid++) {
            if (!local_mget_touched(touched, sid)) continue;
            const uint64_t state = srv_->shard(static_cast<int32_t>(sid))
                                       .store()
                                       .read_local_state_acquire();
            if (FlatStore::read_local_generation_poisoned(state))
                return ReadLocalFallbackReason::Generation;
            window.states[sid] = state;
            // The filter-on path lets each probe perform the topology handshake. The generation
            // control must be even now so an equal even word later proves no bracket ran between.
            if (!window.use_epochs && FlatStore::read_local_table_mutating(state))
                return ReadLocalFallbackReason::SeqChurn;
        }
        if (!window.use_epochs) return ReadLocalFallbackReason::None;
        for (uint32_t key = 0; key < key_count; key++) {
            window.epochs[key] = srv_->shard(shards[key]).store().foreign_read_cell_epoch(
                hashes[key]);
        }
        return ReadLocalFallbackReason::None;
    }

    // All window loads follow every value load. Returns None when every participant is unchanged.
    ReadLocalFallbackReason local_mget_window_close(
            const LocalMgetWindow& window, const uint64_t* touched, const uint64_t* hashes,
            const int32_t* shards, uint32_t key_count) const {
        // Formal seqlock hygiene: keep the value loads above on the near side of the re-reads
        // below. Free on x86.
        std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (!window.use_epochs) {
            for (uint32_t sid = 0; sid < srv_->nshards(); sid++) {
                if (!local_mget_touched(touched, sid)) continue;
                const uint64_t after = srv_->shard(static_cast<int32_t>(sid))
                                           .store()
                                           .read_local_state_acquire();
                if (!FlatStore::read_local_state_eligible(after))
                    return ReadLocalFallbackReason::SeqChurn;
                // A group that published its filter but installed nothing leaves the generation
                // equal and only raises the pending bit; the command linearizes before it.
                if (!FlatStore::read_local_generation_equal(window.states[sid], after))
                    return ReadLocalFallbackReason::Generation;
            }
            return ReadLocalFallbackReason::None;
        }
        for (uint32_t key = 0; key < key_count; key++) {
            if (srv_->shard(shards[key]).store().foreign_read_cell_epoch(hashes[key]) !=
                window.epochs[key])
                return ReadLocalFallbackReason::Generation;
        }
        return ReadLocalFallbackReason::None;
    }

    // After the bounded attempts, prefer the actionable atomic reason if one queried key won the
    // final race; otherwise report the last transient reason observed.
    ReadLocalFallbackReason local_mget_final_reason(
            const Op& op, const uint64_t* hashes, const int32_t* shards, uint32_t key_count,
            bool cached_routes, ReadLocalFallbackReason transient) const {
        for (uint32_t key = 0; key < key_count; key++) {
            const uint64_t hash = cached_routes
                ? hashes[key] : FlatStore::hash_key(op.arg(key + 1));
            const int32_t shard_id = cached_routes
                ? shards[key] : srv_->router().shard_of(hash);
            const FlatStore& store = srv_->shard(shard_id).store();
            const uint64_t state = store.read_local_state_acquire();
            if (store.foreign_read_key_unsafe(state, hash))
                return ReadLocalFallbackReason::AtomicPending;
        }
        return transient;
    }

    // What note_local_read_access() records for a lane-served read. Not the MaxmemoryPolicy enum:
    // every policy that keys on nothing a read changes collapses to None here, so the cold helper
    // dispatches on one byte instead of re-deriving the classification per key.
    static constexpr uint8_t kForeignTouchNone = 0;
    static constexpr uint8_t kForeignTouchLru  = 1;
    static constexpr uint8_t kForeignTouchLfu  = 2;

    // Eviction accounting for one key served on the read-local lane, and the CLIENT NO-TOUCH
    // answer for it. The owner does both for every key it serves (FlatStore::find -> touch(), and
    // the per-task climon_note_no_touch() in execute_task); a lane-served read that did neither
    // made the two paths disagree about what a read MEANS:
    //   * LFU/LRU: a key kept hot purely by lane-served reads was never counted as accessed, so
    //     the victim chooser saw it as the coldest thing in the shard and evicted it FIRST -- the
    //     policy inverted (tests/evict_battery.py lfu, lruclock).
    //   * CLIENT NO-TOUCH: the flag was never consulted here, so "suppressed" and "never looked"
    //     were indistinguishable on the wire (tests/climon2.py, client_no_touch_ops).
    // The call sites gate on maxmemory_enabled_ -- the SAME per-pass byte the owner path tests --
    // so the default posture pays one predicted-not-taken branch per key and never loads the
    // policy, the no-touch bit, or the LRU clock. Out of line and cold: reaching it at all means
    // maxmemory is armed, and then this is a cache-cold decision on a path whose whole point is to
    // stay inside this thread's own lines.
    //
    // The arithmetic below is FlatStore::touch()'s, with the two differences foreignness forces:
    // the logarithmic-increment dice are this thread's own (the store's PRNG belongs to its owner
    // and is not safe to advance from here), and the meta write is one unretried CAS
    // (KvObj::touch_eviction_meta_foreign) rather than the owner's load/store pair, so a lost race
    // costs one approximate touch -- which LRU and LFU tolerate by construction -- and can never
    // corrupt a layout bit. Store-rare by construction: LRU writes only when the key's bucket is
    // stale (once per 256 seconds per key) and LFU only when the
    // increment actually fires, so the foreign RFO into the owner's line is the exception rather
    // than the per-read rule.
    __attribute__((noinline, cold))
    void note_local_read_access(const Op& op, const KvObj* object, uint8_t flags) {
        if (op.no_touch()) { srv_->climon_note_no_touch(); return; }
        KvObj* touched = const_cast<KvObj*>(object);
        const uint8_t meta = static_cast<uint8_t>(flags >> 3);
        if (foreign_touch_policy_ == kForeignTouchLru) {
            if (meta != cached_lru_clock_)
                touched->touch_eviction_meta_foreign(flags, cached_lru_clock_);
            return;
        }
        // Random/TTL/noeviction key on nothing a read changes, so there is nothing to record --
        // but the NO-TOUCH count above still has to happen, exactly as it does on the owner.
        if (foreign_touch_policy_ != kForeignTouchLfu) return;
        uint8_t count = meta ? meta : 5;
        const uint32_t base = count > 5 ? static_cast<uint32_t>(count - 5) : 0;
        const uint32_t denominator = base * 10 + 1;
        uint64_t x = foreign_touch_random_;
        x ^= x >> 12; x ^= x << 25; x ^= x >> 27;
        foreign_touch_random_ = x;
        if (count < 31 && (x * 2685821657736338717ULL) % denominator == 0) count++;
        if (count != meta) touched->touch_eviction_meta_foreign(flags, count);
    }

    // TEST HOOK (DEBUG ATOMIC-FANOUT-DEFER), the read-local half. A fused read-local MGET never
    // enters the scatter engine, so the fan-out park there widens nothing for it and the one
    // expiry-cut invariant expwide.py S1 polices went unexercised on the path that serves every
    // clean MGET in the armed posture. This is the same window on that path: the cut
    // (command_now_ms) is already pinned, no value has been loaded, and the hook holds the lane
    // open between the two. It STALLS rather than parks because the local lane is synchronous --
    // there is no fragment to re-queue and nothing else can run on this thread meanwhile -- and the
    // stall is the point: every key is then read after the wall clock has passed a deadline the
    // pinned cut still says is ahead, which is exactly the tear a per-key clock would produce.
    // Cold and out of line; the caller's test is one thread-private word latched per pass, so an
    // unarmed MGET pays a predicted-not-taken branch and no atomic load (see LiveConfigSnapshot).
    __attribute__((noinline, cold)) void debug_fanout_stall_local() {
        Server::debug_stall_us(debug_fanout_defer_us_);
    }

    PreparedLocalRead prepare_local_mget(Op& op) {

        const uint32_t key_count = op.argc() - 1;
        if (!key_count || srv_->nshards() > LocalMgetWindow::kMaxShards) std::abort();

        uint64_t hashes[LocalMgetWindow::kMaxEpochKeys];

                uint64_t{1} << (static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id) & 63);

                shards[key] = shard_id;

            // copy, giving all stable participant intervals one command-wide intersection.

                window, touched, hashes, shards, key_count, cached_routes);

            if (!retry) reply_array_header(op.sink(), key_count);

                const Slice name = op.arg(key + 1);
                const uint64_t hash = cached_routes ? hashes[key] : FlatStore::hash_key(name);
                const int32_t shard_id = cached_routes
                    ? shards[key] : srv_->router().shard_of(hash);
                FlatStore& store = srv_->shard(shard_id).store();
                store.read_local_prefetch(hash);
                const FlatStore::ReadLocalProbe probe = store.read_local_probe(hash, name);
                if (probe.result == FlatStore::ReadLocalProbeResult::AtomicPending) {
                    read_local_clear_reply(op);
                    return {ReadLocalFallbackReason::AtomicPending};
                }
                if (probe.result == FlatStore::ReadLocalProbeResult::Churn) {
                    transient = ReadLocalFallbackReason::SeqChurn;
                    retry = true;
                    break;
                }
                if (probe.result == FlatStore::ReadLocalProbeResult::Missing) {
                    // Parser admission excludes an armed keymiss notification, whose owner lookup
                    // may emit an event. With that state ruled out, a validated absent slot has no
                    // lazy-expiry side effect and is an ordinary array nil element.
                    reply_null(op.sink(), op.resp3());
                    prepared.keyspace_misses++;
                    if (!window.use_epochs && !store.read_local_validate(probe.state)) {
                        transient = ReadLocalFallbackReason::SeqChurn;
                        retry = true;
                    }
                    continue;
                }

                const KvObj* object = probe.object;
                if (!object) std::abort();
                const uint8_t flags = object->read_local_flags();
                if (static_cast<Type>(object->type) != Type::String) {
                    read_local_clear_reply(op);
                    return {ReadLocalFallbackReason::Typed};
                }
                if (flags & KvObjFlags::HasTtl) {
                    const int64_t deadline = object->read_local_expire_at_ms(flags);
                    if (deadline >= 0 && deadline <= command_now_ms) {
